samples.scenario: Misconfigured Google Cloud Storage bucket with public read access exposes confidential marketing campaign assets which are accessed and downloaded by an unauthorized external party leveraging anonymous access.

technical_data.HTTP_Request_for_object:
GET /marketing-campaign-assets/launch_video.mp4 HTTP/1.1
Host: storage.googleapis.com
User-Agent: curl/7.68.0
Accept: */*
technical_data.Automated_Scanning_Tool_Output:
Scanning bucket marketing-campaign-assets...
Bucket permissions include allUsers with roles/storage.objectViewer.
Bucket is publicly accessible. Enumerated 256 objects.
Downloading launch_video.mp4 - 150MB
Download complete.

indicators: GCS bucket IAM binding granting roles/storage.objectViewer to allUsers
Audit logs showing anonymous principal accessing storage.objects.get method
HTTP GET requests to storage.googleapis.com bucket URLs returning 200 OK for confidential assets
GCS access logs documenting external IP access with user agent curl
Automated tools detecting public read permissions on sensitive GCS buckets
samples.detection_method: Implement Google Cloud Organization Policy constraints to prevent public IAM bindings on storage buckets. Continuously monitor Audit Logs for anonymous or allUsers access events. Employ automated scanning tools to identify publicly accessible buckets and alert on any sensitive data exposure. Analyze GCS access logs for unusual or unauthorized IP addresses and user agents.
relevant_mitre_techniques: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object
T1078 - Valid Accounts (Anonymous access considered valid in this context)
T1081 - Credentials in Files (if credentials stored in bucket)
T1218 - Signed Binary Proxy Execution (for automated tools accessing the bucket)

samples.detection_method: Enforce Azure Storage account policies to restrict public blob access. Utilize Azure Monitor and Azure Security Center to flag public access configurations and audit anonymous blob read operations. Schedule periodic automated scans of blob containers to detect and alert on any containers with public access enabled. Review blob storage logs for access patterns from unexpected IP addresses or user agents.
